other_side: NLW reads this week's launches as a healthy market finding its shape: voice as the next interface, cheap good-enough models for teams building a sensible stack, and a compute crunch that proves demand is real. Zitron's Concentration Risk, three days earlier, says the money underneath that picture is circular. By his reckoning, using Ramp data, eighty per cent of OpenAI and Anthropic's enterprise revenue comes from one per cent of customers, mostly venture-funded AI startups that buy tokens at list price and then subsidise their own users at a loss; he calls them "the NINJA borrowers of AI". Those two labs in turn justify the hyperscalers' capex, and the hyperscalers justify NVIDIA, so a Microsoft 38-gigawatt target or a Huang growth forecast is not evidence of demand but of dependency, with some 200 billion dollars of take-or-pay compute commitments falling due in 2027. Cheaper models are not a comfort in his telling: the tech customers who pay the bills are exactly the ones most likely to defect to good-enough open or self-hosted models, which is more exposure for the labs, not less.
truth_beneath: The variable both men orbit is who is actually paying for the tokens, and whether that payer is durable. Both accept as fact that the subsidy era is ending: NLW quotes Schumer's line approvingly and Zitron's whole essay is about what happens when it does. Both accept that demand currently outruns supply, that Microsoft and NVIDIA are staking five more years of capex on it, and that good-enough models are getting sharply cheaper. The empirical question that will resolve is whether spending survives the subsidy: the observable is whether OpenAI's paused Pro tier and the general repricing of tokens move revenue towards non-tech enterprises, or whether the venture-funded startups that Zitron says make up most of it simply raise less and buy less. The worldview residue is whether a compute wall is a growth signal or a warning. NLW is vindicated if hospitals, banks and small firms keep paying at real prices for voice and vertical tools; Zitron if the 2027 take-or-pay bills arrive with the same one per cent still footing them. Both are polemicists with incentives, one bullish and anti-doom, the other bubble-certain and anti-hype; the signal is that both expect the free-token years to end within months. Watch the revenue mix at OpenAI's next disclosure.
